steps.issue: GAP G8 (clause c), DORMANT. Corrected from a first-pass `deliberate-divergence` whose rationale asserted "same observable ... reached by different routes", which cannot both hold: the two guards do not test the same predicate. C#'s check is an artifact of positional overload resolution — overload #1 accepts a repeatType but has no maxRepeats slot, so CanRepeatXTimes must be rejected there and expressed through overload #2 instead. The sim's add_branch is a single keyword signature in which max_times is always addressable, so C#'s guard is INAPPLICABLE: the sim has no analogue of it. The ValueError the sim raises on the closest transliteration comes from an unrelated predicate, max_times <= 0, which is a WIDER guard that also rejects AddBranch(state, 0) — a construction C# ACCEPTS (step 21, G7 clause a). So the sim's apparent coverage of C#'s guard is incidental to a different divergence, and it would DISAPPEAR the moment step 21 were fixed toward the game: a sim that permanently disabled a max_times==0 branch as C# does would then silently accept the very construction C# rejects here. Bucketed by probe raise-sites as the one ONE-SIDED-GUARD site (only C# guards it deliberately). Same mechanism and therefore the same verdict as steps 3 and 37 (rule 3); see step 3 for the shared statement. Dormant: probe cs-addbranch resolves all 61 monster call sites and none uses overload #1 with CanRepeatXTimes (1 site uses #1 at all) and none passes 0 as maxRepeats. Named trigger: the same one as step 21 — a C# monster added with AddBranch(state, 0) or a cooldown+CanRepeatXTimes call written against overload #1.
